tools.name: todays_specials
tools.description: Live security incidents right now (CVEs, breaches, supply-chain compromises) with severity, patch status, fixed versions and ids. Pass stack ids to see only what touches your stack. Known ids: nextjs, react, node, bun, php, python, ruby, go, java, wordpress, drupal, magento, perl, proof-tools, dotne

tools.name: lookup_cve
tools.description: The incident covering a CVE or GHSA id, or a named bug (e.g. HTTP2Shell): summary, severity, patch status, fixed versions, timeline and sources.

tools.name: check_lockfile
tools.description: Match the packages and versions in a lockfile against incidents that state fixed versions, and print a receipt: what you use, the version, affected or not, and the exact upgrade. Accepts package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, requirements.txt, poetry.lock, uv.lock, Pipfile.lock, composer.lock

tools.name: check_repo
tools.description: Send the files that describe what a project runs (lockfiles, Dockerfiles, .github/workflows/*.yml, wrangler.toml, vercel.json, next.config.*, compose files) in one call. Returns one receipt: every affected package with the exact command to fix it in the tool the repo already uses, actions and images

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description: Incidents created or updated since a point in time, newest first. Use it to re-check only what changed since your last run. Accepts "24h", "7d", "90m" or an ISO timestamp.

tools.name: diff_since
tools.description: Every correction, new ticket and fix-status change since a point in time, each with the source behind it (the same log as /corrections). Use it to audit what the board changed since your last run. Accepts an ISO 8601 timestamp, or "24h", "7d", "90m".

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "todays_specials" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
